title: Three walks stop before the thing they were written to check
goal: Three of the scripted walks that the loop uses to prove the app still works stop partway: the two that open the capture history and the one that checks a mark parked outside a clipped box. Nobody is being told whether those parts of the app still behave, because the walks never reach them.
notes: From the full sweep on 2026-09-07 (221 passed, 15 failed; the other twelve are the colour style naming regression, filed separately). history-menu-title-walk: step 9, 'Capture > Show History is not ticked and it should be ticked before command+shift+h'. history-tooltips-walk: step 5, no window called 'Capture History' is open. out-of-view-mark-walk: step 27, the control 'Clip contents' is not in the window, so it needs a scrollPanel step first (that one is almost certainly the walk, not the app). Run one with Scripts/playtest.sh <walk>; run the lot with Scripts/playtest-all.sh.
acceptance: history-menu-title-walk, history-tooltips-walk and out-of-view-mark-walk each run to the end and report ok
Each one still checks what it was written for, or says in its notes what was dropped and why
If a walk stops because the app is wrong rather than the walk, the app is fixed instead

log.note: Reproduced each one on its own with Scripts/playtest.sh. out-of-view-mark-walk fails every time. The two history walks PASS on their own: 12 runs in a row, plus a run of the same five walks the sweep ran in that order, all green.

Adversarial read before touching anything. out-of-view-mark: opening the Card in the layers list adds four rows to the one scrolling dock column, which pushes the Layout section below the fold, so the last press cannot reach Clip contents. The walk is wrong, not the app, but the underlying squeeze is real and worth a look on its own: the layers list and the inspector share one column, so opening a group can shove a control you were using off screen.

out-of-view-mark-walk fixed: scroll the dock down to the Layout section, untick Clip contents, scroll back up. Stage 4 still reads the mark off the Body row (it says 'layer' where stage 3 said 'layer, out of view, cut off by Card'), so the check it was written for survives.

The two history walks are not broken, they are reachable from outside. The capture history overlay closes on any mouse-down in ANOTHER app, and the probe registers system-wide Carbon hotkeys including the real command+shift+H. During the 2026-09-06 sweep the user was working on the same machine (they committed at 23:19, the sweep ran at 23:01), so one click or one command+shift+H aimed at their own Photonz took the overlay down mid-walk. That matches both failures exactly: the menu-title walk got its picture at step 8 and found the item unticked at step 9, and the tooltips walk found no overlay at all. No code touching the overlay or the menus changed between that sweep and now.

Fix: AppFlavor.claimsInputOutsideItself (PhotonzCore, tested). The probe no longer registers the system-wide capture/history hotkeys and no longer installs the click-in-another-app dismiss monitor. Escape and click-away inside the app still take the overlay down, which is what the walks actually exercise, and the dev and release builds are untouched. Also gave the tooltips walk a checked:false guard on its command+shift+H so an already-open overlay fails at the shortcut with a plain message instead of confusingly at a snapshot two steps later.

Honest limit: the outside click could not be reproduced on demand (driving another app needs the Accessibility grant, which this terminal does not have), so the cause is inference from the evidence rather than a reproduction. The hardening covers both ways in.

All three walks run to the end and report ok, twice in a row, and green alongside every menu walk (8 passed, 0 failed). out-of-view-mark-walk was the only broken one and the walk was at fault: opening the Card in the layers list pushed the Layout section below the fold, so it now scrolls to Clip contents and back, and stage 4 still reads the mark off the Body row. The two history walks were never broken; they were reachable from outside, so the probe now registers none of the system-wide capture hotkeys and does not close the capture history when a click lands in another app (AppFlavor.claimsInputOutsideItself, PhotonzCore, tested). Dev and release untouched. Suite green at 4268. Committed as 52f77241.
